sections.title: Where Things Are
sections.content: 'Hay' says that something exists. 'Estar' says where it is. So a place you are mentioning for the first time takes 'hay' — 'hay un café' — and once you both know which café you mean, it takes 'estar': 'el café está al lado del lago'. Unlike 'hay', 'estar' changes with who or what you are talking about.

items.spanish: El café está al lado del lago.
items.english: The café is next to the lake.

items.spanish: Los sábados el mercado está muy lleno.
items.english: On Saturdays the market is very crowded.

items.spanish: Las librerías están en el barrio antiguo.
items.english: The bookshops are in the old quarter.

sections.content: 'De' and 'el' always contract to 'del': 'al lado del lago', never 'al lado de el lago'. The same happens with 'a': 'a el' becomes 'al'.
